1 --- 2 title: forbidden 3 description: API Reference for the forbidden function. 4 version: experimental 5 related: 6 links: 7 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden 8 - app/api-reference/functions/not-found 9 - app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized 10 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts 11 --- 12 13 The `forbidden` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 403 page. It's useful for handling authorization errors in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`forbidden.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden). 14 15 Invoking `forbidden()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;403` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no forbidden UI renders. 16 17 To start using `forbidden`, enable the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) configuration option in your `next.config.js` file: 18 19 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 20 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 21 22 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 23 experimental: { 24 authInterrupts: true, 25 }, 26 } 27 28 export default nextConfig 29 ``` 30 31 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 32 module.exports = { 33 experimental: { 34 authInterrupts: true, 35 }, 36 } 37 ``` 38 39 `forbidden` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 40 41 ```tsx filename="app/admin/page.tsx" switcher 42 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 43 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 44 45 export default async function AdminPage() { 46 const session = await verifySession() 47 48 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 49 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 50 forbidden() 51 } 52 53 // Render the admin page for authorized users 54 return <> 55 } 56 ``` 57 58 ```jsx filename="app/admin/page.js" switcher 59 import { verifySession } from '@/app/lib/dal' 60 import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' 61 62 export default async function AdminPage() { 63 const session = await verifySession() 64 65 // Check if the user has the 'admin' role 66 if (session.role !== 'admin') { 67 forbidden() 68 } 69 70 // Render the admin page for authorized users 71 return <> 72 } 73 ``` 74 75 ## Good to know 76 77 - The `forbidden` function cannot be called in the [root layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout). 78 - You do not need to write `return forbidden()`. Use [`unstable_rethrow`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_rethrow) to let it through. 79 - A `forbidden()` left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, so no forbidden UI renders. In development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;403`. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), every dynamic route streams a static shell first, so run that check in [`proxy`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) instead. See [Status codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes). 186 187 ### Role-based route protection 188 189 You can use `forbidden` to restrict access to certain routes based on user roles.
